metaDescription: Every Indian bank account on one screen. Upload a statement and Horizon finds hidden bank charges, every EMI by lender, bills and subscriptions. 7 days free.
heroBody: Every bank account, balance and transaction on one calm screen. Upload a statement or connect a bank; Horizon sorts the spending, spots the bills and keeps your savings goals in view.
trust: Statements are read once and never stored. Horizon never asks for your net-banking password.
cap1Body: Upload a PDF, Excel or CSV statement from any bank, or connect one. Every balance sits together, each in its own currency.
cap2Body: UPI, cards, EMIs and pay-later settlements are grouped on their own. Correct a label once and Horizon remembers it.
cap3Title: Bills and goals that stay on track
cap3Body: Subscriptions and recurring bills are found in your statements, with what is due next. Savings goals show how far along you are.
cap4Body: Minimum-balance penalties, SMS and card fees, ATM and bounce charges: every rupee your bank took this year, with a ready request to ask for it back.
cap5Body: Banks, NBFCs, loan apps and pay later, each by name: what each takes a month, how much of your income goes to EMIs, and which loan to close first.
cap6Title: Each kind of spending, up close
cap6Body: Open UPI, food or shopping to see who the money went to, month by month, the days it goes out, and how this month compares with usual.
f1Body: Your total across banks, where the money sits, and this month's spending by type, with your bank cards beside them. One glance, nothing to configure.
f2Title: Upload a statement, get it sorted
f2Body: Drop a statement from your net banking, password and all. Horizon checks it with you before saving, then sorts every entry: EMIs, pay-later, groceries, subscriptions, transfers.
f3Body: Netflix, Crunchyroll, YouTube, Airtel, the electricity bill: Horizon spots what recurs in your statements and lines up what is due next, so nothing surprises you.
f4Body: An emergency fund, a trip, a down payment. Set a target and a monthly amount, and watch each one fill up as your balances grow.
priceTitle: {days} days free, then {monthly} a month or {yearly} a year.
priceBody: No card to start. Cancel any time; access lasts to the end of the paid period. Seeing, downloading and deleting your data is always free.
closingBody: Take back the overview that a dozen bank apps keep from you.
shotHome: Horizon's home page: the total across banks, a doughnut of where the money sits, spending by type and the bank cards
shotHistory: Horizon's account history: entries sorted into categories, with inflow, outflow and net for the month
shotBills: Horizon's bills page: subscriptions and recurring bills found in the statements, with what is due next
shotGoals: Horizon's savings goals, each with a target and progress
shotConnect: Horizon's connect-a-bank page: upload a statement, then check it before saving
shotHero: The top of Horizon's landing page: the name over three screens of the app
shotPhone: Horizon's home page on a phone
cap7Body: A forecast from your pay day to the next: what has already happened, what is due, and the day the balance might dip below zero. A calendar lays it out.
cap8Title: A health score and a monthly report
cap8Body: One number for how the month went, and the parts behind it: EMIs against income, what is spoken for before the month starts, what was left.
cap9Title: Learns from you, in your language
cap9Body: When Horizon is unsure it asks: your salary? your own transfer? which subscription? Each answer sharpens the charts. Eleven Indian languages.
f5Body: Minimum-balance penalties, SMS and card fees, ATM and bounce charges: every rupee the bank took, by kind and by month, with a ready-made request to ask for it back.
f6Body: Banks, NBFCs, loan apps and pay later: what each takes a month, how much of your income goes to EMIs, which loan to close first, and your subscriptions beside them.
f7Body: A forecast from your pay day to the next: what has already happened, what is due, where the balance is heading. The calendar shows salary day, EMI days and bill days at a glance.
f8Title: A health score for the month
f8Body: One number for how the month went, and the parts behind it: EMIs against income, what is spoken for before the month starts, what was left over. A reminder brings you back each week.
shotCharges: Horizon's bank charges page: every fee by kind and by month, with a request to the bank
shotLoans: Horizon's EMIs and loans page: each lender and what it takes a month
shotCalendar: Horizon's cash-flow calendar: salary, EMIs and bills on their days, with the balance forecast
shotReport: Horizon's monthly report: the health score and the parts behind it
shotSpending: Horizon's page for one kind of spending: who the money went to, month by month, and the days it goes out
shotChecks: Horizon's quick checks: the questions it asks when a payment is unclear
cap10Body: Netflix, YouTube, the gym, and your Jio or Airtel plan: what each costs, what they add up to a month, which quietly stopped, and when the next recharge is due.
f9Body: Every subscription found in your statements, running or stopped, with what they cost a month and a year. Under them, your prepaid mobile and DTH plans: the plan you are on, when it runs out, and what a month really costs.
shotSubscriptions: Horizon's subscriptions and recharges page: each subscription with its monthly cost, and each prepaid plan with its next due date
